answer: One defence is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a refundable deposit and build a verifiable history before its votes count fully. A single good deed should not ripple into full trust overnight; instead trust grows mesa-steady, layer by layer, as peers attest real work. Creating thousands of fake identities then means funding thousands of deposits, while a velvet-smooth flood of empty accounts with no history stays easy to discount. Attack cost scales with every identity, honest cost stays one deposit.
